correctness.rationale: The forbidden disconnected-four-set predicate is exactly the Alexander dual of the ordinary four-cut complex. Its rectangular-core decomposition and distinct-column transversal triangles are exhaustively classified by incidence connectivity. Sequential row-major matching is acyclic by the first-pivot argument; the column-extension case analysis yields exactly 2 C(n-1,3)+C(n,3) critical 3-faces and one vertex in the core. Each additional transversal triangle attaches along a nullhomotopic circle because the core has only 0- and 3-cells, giving the integral S2 and S3 wedge. Integral Alexander duality yields the specified original homology. Complete direct finite reconstructions (n=3..6), critical-face identity (n=3..8), acyclic Hasse checks (n=3..7), and independent mod-2 ranks (n=3..6) corroborate but do not replace the uniform combinatorial induction.
